references.text: Mentions that the fathers went down to Egypt with seventy people, and now the Lord has made them as numerous as the stars in the sky - the same motif of the people's multitude like the stars.
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants will become as numerous as the stars in the sky - the basis for the comparison in Deuteronomy 28:62.
Reiteration of the promise to Abraham that his offspring will become as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.
Moses says that the Lord has made the Israelites as numerous as the stars in the sky - a contrast to the judgment in 28:62 where they are reduced to few.
Warns that the people will be scattered among the nations and only a small remnant will remain - the same theme of reduction in number.
Isaiah says that if the Lord had not left a small remnant, they would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah - the theme that only a remnant survives.
Nehemiah refers to the promise that Abraham's descendants will become as numerous as the stars - the same background for the comparison.
Moses reminds God of the promise to the fathers that their offspring will become as numerous as the stars in the sky.
